niche: Residential Rooftop Solar + Solar Battery + EV Charging (Chennai, TN)
spend: Rs.1-3 L/mo (est. - verify in Meta Ad Library)
pitch_fit: HIGH - regional residential EPC, 100+ cities, subsidy-led category, no WhatsApp CTA
ad_intro:
Fenice Energy (SILRES Energy Solutions Pvt Ltd, Chennai) sells rooftop solar, solar batteries and EV chargers across 100+ cities, with micro-inverters as its technical differentiator. The product and the site hold up - there is a solar calculator, a financing options page and a channel-partner program.

But the highest-intent hook in this category is missing from the first screen. PM Surya Ghar pays Rs.78,000 on a 3 kW residential system plus 300 free units/month. Competitors like Freyr Energy lead with 'Save Rs.1 Lakh' and SolarSquare leads with subsidy + EMI math; Fenice's homepage headline is 'Clean energy for your home & business' - no subsidy, no number, no urgency.

Two more leaks: there is no click-to-WhatsApp path (only a toll-free number), and the installation proof and reviews are buried in the About page while the hero carries no customer evidence for a Rs.1.5-3 lakh purchase.

Findings below are from a live review of the site on 14 Sep 2026. Ad counts and spend are estimates from the Ad Library signature - verify before quoting.
ad_intelligence: PM Surya Ghar: Rs.30,000 (1 kW) / Rs.60,000 (2 kW) / Rs.78,000 (3 kW+) + up to 300 free units/month. This is the highest-intent hook in Indian residential solar right now.
Meta (FB + IG) for residential lead gen; Google Search / PMax on 'solar panel price Chennai', 'PM Surya Ghar subsidy', 'rooftop solar Chennai'; YouTube for install walkthroughs.
~12 creatives by signature. Confirm live count in Meta Ad Library India (Active filter) before the pitch - never quote an unverified number.
Website lead popup ('I am looking for: Residential / Apartment Complex / Commercial') + toll-free number. No WhatsApp entry point observed on the homepage.
Solar rooftop calculator at /solar-rooftop-calculator/, financing options page, micro-inverter product pages, GreenPartners channel program, blog.
Freyr Energy: subsidy + Rs.22,000 discount stacked, 3-step quote form, 4,473 Google reviews on the hero, EMI from Rs.1,466/mo. SolarSquare: city landing pages + EMI/subsidy math on first screen.
Feb-Jun (summer bills, subsidy push) and Sep-Oct (post-monsoon) are peak enquiry months. Tamil Nadu has a strong residential base and active DISCOM net-metering flow.
findings: 1. The subsidy is absent from the first screen. Homepage hero reads 'Clean energy for your home & business' with the sub-line 'Rooftop Solar | Solar Battery | EV Charging'. Nowhere above the fold does it say Rs.78,000 subsidy, 300 free units or 'PM Surya Ghar'. Freyr Energy and SolarSquare both lead with the money. In a subsidy-driven category, the number IS the hook.

2. No click-to-WhatsApp. The only fast contact path is a toll-free number (1800 889 8457). Indian solar enquiries start as questions - 'kitna kharcha?', 'how much roof do I need?', 'subsidy kab milega?' - and those users do not call a toll-free line at 9pm. Competitors capture them on WhatsApp and reply in minutes.

3. Proof is buried. Customer reviews live inside the About Us page, the counters read '0 +' before scroll-triggered animation, and the footer still says Copyright 2023. For a Rs.1.5-3 lakh, 25-year purchase, the hero should carry installations, cities, MW done and a real customer face.

4. The calculator is 2 clicks deep. /solar-rooftop-calculator/ is genuinely good (it can show system size, savings, roof space, subsidy) but it sits in the footer menu. It should be the hero CTA - 'Check your subsidy + savings in 30 seconds' - with the phone number captured after the value is shown.

5. No retargeting journey for a 30-90 day decision. Rooftop solar is rarely a same-day conversion. Without video-view retargeting (50%+) and a WhatsApp follow-up sequence across 60 days, the traffic is rented rather than owned.

6. Channel-partner lever unused for paid. GreenPartners and GreenAmbassadors programs already exist - these are natural sources of zero-CPL referrals that can be amplified with a partner-specific creative track at a fraction of cold-audience CPL.
competitors: Leads with 'Save Rs.1 Lakh' (Rs.78,000 subsidy + Rs.22,000 own discount), shows 4,473 Google reviews above the fold, EMI from Rs.1,466/mo, and a 3-step quote flow.
Fenice should match the money-on-screen pattern, then win on micro-inverters + O&M credibility.
City-level landing pages, financing/EMI clarity, brand-level trust marketing at scale.
Fenice can beat them in Tamil Nadu locality-by-locality (Adyar, Velachery, Anna Nagar) where national brands are thin.
Click-to-WhatsApp as primary CTA, fast quotes, heavy Google review collection.
Speed-to-lead under 5 minutes on WhatsApp is the battleground - not price.
wins: Subsidy-first creative + Click-to-WhatsApp. Test 3 hooks: (a) 'Rs.78,000 subsidy on 3 kW rooftop solar - pay less than your EB bill', (b) '300 units free every month', (c) 'Chennai homeowner: your 25-year bill vs your one-time cost'. Primary CTA = Send WhatsApp Message. Expected: 25-40% more qualified enquiries at the same spend.

Turn the existing calculator into the hero CTA: 'Check your subsidy + savings in 30 seconds' - bill size, city, roof type - show subsidy, EMI and payback, THEN ask for the phone number. Replace the current popup. Expected: 1.5-2x form completion and a higher site-survey booking rate.

Build the proof layer for a 25-year purchase: 10 install films (roof + net meter + customer holding the bill), city-wise install counters, Google review screenshots in creatives, and a 60-day retargeting sequence (video 50% -> WhatsApp -> site-survey offer). Expected: lower CPL and a higher survey-to-order rate.
impact: EMI + subsidy math shown at survey
